source: Qiu et al. (2026) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in Large Language Models
finding: Off-the-shelf LLMs fall far short of an exact Bayesian assistant in a 5-round flight-preference task. Most plateau after round 1 instead of improving as evidence accumulates.
numbers: Task: 5 rounds, 3 flights per round, 624 possible simulated users, 100 held-out option sets scored per round. Many models tested; accuracy values are plotted in figures, not stated in text.
quote: LLMs' performance often plateaus after a single interaction
limits: Exact accuracies are only in figures (not read as numbers). Simulated users, one task family.
agent_relevance: A model asked to update over several rounds of evidence does not accumulate it. Do the update in code (S7), not in the model's head.

source: Qiu et al. (2026) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in Large Language Models
finding: Chain-of-thought prompting, numeric flight encodings, 30 rounds instead of 5, and other prompt-side fixes did not give meaningful improvement in Bayesian updating.
numbers: Appendix C.1 lists the failed interventions: CoT, purely numerical representation, 30-round setting.
quote: A range of follow-up experiments failed to produce meaningful improvement
limits: Text reports no improvement; effect sizes in appendix figures.
agent_relevance: Prompt tricks do not fix belief updating. Supports moving normalisation and updating into code.

source: Qiu et al. (2026) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in Large Language Models
finding: Fine-tuning Gemma 2 9B, Llama 3 8B and Qwen 2.5 7B to imitate a Bayesian Assistant made them improve across rounds and agree with the Bayesian model about 80% of the time. Imitating the Bayesian guesses beat imitating the oracle (always-correct) answers.
numbers: 10 five-round interactions per user for training; 3 seeds; all differences p<0.001; Bayesian-tuned agreement with Bayesian Assistant around 80%.
quote: Bayesian teaching leads to higher accuracy and less variability across repetitions of the experiment than oracle teaching
limits: Needs fine-tuning, so not usable in a scaffold-only agent. Teacher early guesses are often wrong yet still teach better.
agent_relevance: Shows updating is learnable but our agent cannot train. Evidence that explicit posterior values (not just answers) carry the signal.

source: Qiu et al. (2026) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in Large Language Models
finding: Bayesian-tuned models generalised to hotel recommendation and a real web-shopping task never seen in training. Verbalised beliefs (asking for a 1-5 preference rating, then deriving the recommendation) gave better recommendations than asking for the recommendation directly.
numbers: Models: Gemma 2 9B, Llama 3 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B. Tasks: flight variants, hotel, web shopping.
limits: Direct accuracy figures not in text. Fine-tuned models only.
agent_relevance: Ask for explicit belief values, then let code decide. Matches S7 design.

source: Qiu et al. (2026) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in Large Language Models
finding: Human participants acting as the assistant (48 simulated users) improved from round 1 to round 5 (p=0.002) and beat small LLMs, but humans also fell well short of the Bayesian strategy.
numbers: N: 48 simulated users, 5 rounds, logistic mixed-effects model p=0.002.
limits: Small human sample; humans slightly worse than larger LLMs.
agent_relevance: Both humans and LLMs are non-Bayesian updaters, so code normalisation is a gain over either.

source: Gupta et al. (2025) Enough Coin Flips Can Make LLMs Act Bayesian
finding: With a biased-coin task, LLMs have biased priors (about 60-80% heads regardless of the stated bias), ignore explicit bias statements in the prompt, but with enough in-context flips their outputs follow a Bayesian posterior mean.
numbers: Models: Llama-3.1-8B and Instruct, Pythia 70M to 12B. Explicit statement of heads X% of the time failed for non-instruct models. 100-step switching trajectory: theta 0.75 for 50 flips then 0.25 for 50.
quote: in-context evidence outweighs explicit bias instructions
limits: Simple Bernoulli task. Deviations are mostly in the prior, not the update rule.
agent_relevance: Evidence shown in context beats stated priors. Give the model data, not assertions about rates.

source: Gupta et al. (2025) Enough Coin Flips Can Make LLMs Act Bayesian
finding: Scale did not fix this: larger Pythia models were not better at using in-context evidence; the 12B model often had higher total variation distance than smaller ones. Attention magnitude had negligible effect on update quality.
numbers: Pythia 70M to 12B, theta=0.20 setting; correlation of attention with calibration R=0.02 (p=0.48) and R=-0.03 (p=0.36).
limits: Pythia is a base model family; instruct models were only slightly better at extremes (0% and 100% bias).
agent_relevance: Do not assume a bigger model normalises better.

source: Arora et al. (2025) Bayesian scaling laws for in-context learning
finding: In-context learning can be fit by a Bayesian scaling law with interpretable terms for task prior, learning efficiency and per-example probability. It matches existing scaling laws in accuracy (NRMSE) on GPT-2 sized models.
numbers: Fit and extrapolation compared by normalised RMSE across GPT-2 sizes and trajectory lengths. Also predicts many-shot jailbreak re-emergence after SFT/DPO suppression.
limits: Fitted on small models plus instruction-tuned LLM checks. Descriptive fit, not proof the model is Bayesian.
agent_relevance: Fine-tuning may only reweight priors. More evidence in context can revive an answer the model had dropped, so keep suppressed candidates in the harvest.

source: Xie et al. (2022) An Explanation of In-context Learning as Implicit Bayesian Inference
finding: Theory: if the prompt concept is distinguishable from other concepts, in-context prediction approaches Bayes-optimal as examples grow. On the synthetic GINC data, Transformers and LSTMs show ICL that improves with more and longer examples.
numbers: Accuracy rises with number of examples and example length in GINC. For concepts not in the pretraining family, ICL fails (Fig. 4 right). Accuracy varies widely with example order (Fig. 7).
limits: Synthetic data, small models. Needs a distinguishability condition.
agent_relevance: Conditionalization-like behaviour needs distinguishable hypotheses. Keep candidate answers distinct before selection.

source: Xie et al. (2022) An Explanation of In-context Learning as Implicit Bayesian Inference
finding: Zero-shot can beat few-shot in some GINC settings, because the few-shot prompt format adds distracting structure. This mirrors GPT-3 on LAMBADA.
numbers: Fig. 7 right (GINC).
limits: Synthetic setting.
agent_relevance: Extra context is not always more evidence; format noise can lower accuracy.

source: Zhao et al. (2021) Calibrate Before Use: Improving Few-Shot Performance of Language Models
finding: GPT-3 few-shot answer probabilities carry a bias toward majority label, recency and common tokens. Rescaling with a content-free input (N/A) so predictions are uniform raises accuracy.
numbers: Gains up to 30.0% absolute. SST-2 4-shot GPT-3 2.7B: permutation of the same examples moved accuracy from 54.3% to 93.4%. 4-shot LAMA: 50.2% of predictions repeat a prompt answer; correct repeat rate 24.7%. Models GPT-3 2.7B/13B/175B and GPT-2 1.5B.
limits: GPT-3 era, classification tasks.
agent_relevance: Renormalising answer probabilities against a content-free prior is a conditionalization-style fix. Run it in code before voting.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
finding: Aggregating sampled answers by (length-normalised) probability weights or by majority vote beats single greedy chain-of-thought. The normalised weighted sum was much better than the unnormalised one; unweighted vote was about as good as normalised weighting because sample probabilities were nearly equal.
numbers: Gains +3-6% absolute for UL2-20B, +9-23% for LaMDA-137B and GPT-3, +12-18% on AQuA and GSM8K for large models (GPT-3, PaLM-540B), +7-11% on SVAMP and ASDiv.
limits: Needs a fixed answer set; model likelihoods are poorly informative about correctness.
agent_relevance: Mass over exclusive answers is best computed by code from counts. Matches G5.

source: Zheng et al. (2024) Large Language Models Are Not Robust Multiple Choice Selectors
finding: LLMs put prior probability mass on particular option letters. Moving the correct answer to a fixed position changes accuracy a lot. PriDe estimates the letter prior from a few permuted samples and divides it out.
numbers: MMLU 0-shot: gold moved to D drops gpt-3.5-turbo from 67.2 to 60.9; gold moved to A lifts llama-30B by 15.2 (68.2 vs 53.1 original) so it passes gpt-3.5-turbo (65.3). With 250 of each correct letter, llama-30B picks A/B/C/D 34.6/27.3/22.3/15.8%. 20 LLMs, 3 benchmarks.
limits: MCQ format; a prior-correction, not a full posterior.
agent_relevance: When an answer set is mapped to letters, divide out the position prior and shuffle. Same logic as dividing a prior from a likelihood.

source: Feng et al. (2025) BIRD: A Trustworthy Bayesian Inference Framework for Large Language Models
finding: BIRD has the LLM propose factors and coarse judgments, then fits an explicit Bayesian network and computes conditional probabilities in code. Its probabilities match human preference better than direct LLM probability statements.
numbers: Pairwise preference F1 of 59% for both base models, more than 30% above GPT-4; still 5% above GPT-4 when GPT-4 sees both conditions at once. Used Llama-2-70b and Llama-3.1.
limits: Beats CoT only on some decision benchmarks (clearly on the hardest, TODAY); comparable or slightly worse on others. Needs 128 training instances per scenario.
agent_relevance: A working example of an LLM agent loop where the Bayesian update is done outside the model. Directly the S7 pattern.

source: Zhu & Griffiths (2024) Eliciting the Priors of Large Language Models using Iterated In-Context Learning
finding: Chaining GPT-4 predictions (iterated learning) samples its prior. Elicited priors on causal strength, proportion and everyday quantities qualitatively matched human priors.
numbers: Causal task: 100 chains, 12 iterations each (25 random starts x 4 seeds), chains reached a stationary distribution by iterations 7 and 8. Proportion task with p(Head) in {0.3,0.5,0.7}.
limits: Qualitative agreement only; GPT-4 only.
agent_relevance: A way to measure what prior the model brings before it sees evidence. Useful as an audit, not as a runtime step.

source: Lew et al. (2023) Sequential Monte Carlo Steering of Large Language Models using Probabilistic Programs
finding: Treats constraints as conditioning: generation becomes posterior inference, with a hard condition setting violating continuations to zero and probability mass redistributed over the rest. Token masking alone cannot do this because it cannot see future violations.
numbers: Demo with LLaMA-7B: prompt The Fed says, constraint no word over five letters; a two-token completion had log probability -11.74 yet was more likely than any single long completion.
limits: Workshop abstract, qualitative demo, no accuracy benchmark.
agent_relevance: Literal conditionalization inside decoding: zero out what the check rules out, renormalise. Closest direct analogue of S4 to S7.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) Probabilistic Inference in Language Models via Twisted Sequential Monte Carlo
finding: Casts RLHF-style steering, red-teaming and infilling as sampling from an unnormalised target; learned twist functions focus compute on promising partial sequences, and bidirectional SMC bounds estimate KL between sampler and target.
numbers: Applied to sampling undesirable outputs, varied-sentiment reviews and infilling.
limits: Needs training twist functions; numbers are in tables not extracted here.
agent_relevance: Method for conditioning a generator on a property; too heavy for scaffold-only use but shows the posterior framing.

source: Halawi et al. (2024) Approaching Human-Level Forecasting with Language Models
finding: With no retrieval, almost all of 14 LMs score near or worse than a coin-flip forecast. With news retrieval, prompt optimisation and aggregation, the system nears the human crowd.
numbers: Brier score: no-retrieval baseline best GPT-4-1106-Preview .208 vs crowd .149 (random = .25). Full system .179 vs crowd .149; accuracy 71.5% vs crowd 77.0%.
limits: Binary questions; test set after training cutoff.
agent_relevance: Probability updating on new evidence helps only when evidence is supplied and results are aggregated in code.

source: Kadavath et al. (2022) Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
finding: Large models are well calibrated on multiple-choice and true/false items when formatted properly. Calibration improves with size and few-shot prompting. Self-evaluation P(True) improves when the model sees many of its own samples first.
numbers: Tested at scale up to 52B on TriviaQA, Lambada, arithmetic, GSM8k, Codex HumanEval; answers with P(True)>50% were far more often correct.
quote: brainstorming other possibilities helps large models to evaluate the validity of a given answer option
limits: Pure LMs; calibration worsens out of distribution; RLHF policy checked only briefly.
agent_relevance: Model probabilities can serve as likelihood inputs, if formatted as multiple choice. Seeing alternatives first helps.

source: Tian et al. (2023) Just Ask for Calibration
finding: For RLHF models (ChatGPT, GPT-4, Claude) verbalised confidence is better calibrated than the token probabilities, often cutting expected calibration error by a relative 50%. RLHF worsens calibration of log probabilities.
numbers: TriviaQA, SciQ, TruthfulQA; Llama-70B comparison of ECE and AUC.
limits: Calibration measured on QA benchmarks only.
agent_relevance: If the agent needs a likelihood number from a chat model, ask for a stated probability, not the logprob.

source: Binz & Schulz (2023) Using cognitive psychology to understand GPT-3
finding: GPT-3 did not show the human base-rate fallacy on the cab problem and gave approximately the correct answer. It answered 12 of 12 standard vignettes correctly or with human-like errors, but failed small rewordings.
numbers: Cab problem (base rate of taxi colours); 12 of 12 vignettes; Linda problem also run.
limits: Famous vignettes are probably in training data; small perturbations broke it.
agent_relevance: Textbook Bayes problems are a poor test of updating; use novel tasks.

source: Hagendorff et al. (2023) Thinking Fast and Slow in Large Language Models
finding: Earlier GPT-3 models showed human-like intuitive errors on the cognitive reflection test and semantic illusions, while ChatGPT and GPT-4 mostly avoided them by chain-of-thought-like reasoning.
numbers: Not extracted as exact percentages in this pass.
limits: Exact figures not captured here.
agent_relevance: Newer models are less intuition-driven but still err on novel framings.

source: Paruchuri et al. (2024) What Are the Odds? Language Models Are Capable of Probabilistic Reasoning
finding: Gemini 1.0 Ultra, GPT-4-Turbo and GPT-3.5-Turbo were tested on percentiles, sampling and probabilities for 12 idealised distributions. Real-world context, example shots and even wrong Normal approximations helped.
numbers: Three tasks, three models, default temperature 0.7.
limits: Single distribution questions, not sequential updating.
agent_relevance: Giving summary statistics helps even when approximate; supply numbers to the model.

source: Edwards (1968) Conservatism in human information processing
finding: Classic finding that people revise probabilities less than Bayes rule says (conservatism).
numbers: Not read this session; figures not recorded.
limits: From memory, unverified.
agent_relevance: Human baseline: humans under-update, so human-style prompting is not a good model for the target.

source: Casscells, Schoenberger, Graboys (1978) Interpretation by physicians of clinical laboratory results
finding: Most physicians ignored the base rate in a false-positive test question.
numbers: Not read this session; exact proportions not recorded here.
limits: From memory, unverified.
agent_relevance: Base-rate neglect is the standard failure the update rule is meant to prevent.

source: Gigerenzer & Hoffrage (1995) How to improve Bayesian reasoning without instruction: frequency formats
finding: Natural-frequency formats raised correct Bayesian answers compared with probability formats.
numbers: Not read; figures not recorded.
limits: From memory, unverified. Debated by later work.
agent_relevance: Present counts, not percentages, when the model must combine evidence.

source: Lewis/Teller (1973) diachronic Dutch book argument for conditionalization
finding: Argument that an agent who updates by any rule other than conditionalization can be made to accept a sure loss.
numbers: Not applicable.
limits: From memory; the argument has known critics (for example about learning that is not certain).
agent_relevance: Justifies code-side normalisation.

source: Pearl (1988) Probabilistic Reasoning in Intelligent Systems
finding: Bayesian networks operationalise conditionalization in AI systems.
numbers: Not applicable.
limits: From memory.
agent_relevance: Old AI precedent for BIRD-style design.
